relayHandshake.proof: device signature over authenticated user/device/connection/purpose/session/incarnation and fresh 32-byte challenge
relayHandshake.authorization: host and relay: the publication's hosting device; participant: an approved device of the owner or of an explicit current member

relay.join: the hosting device opens the relay route for the channel within 10 seconds; the server then copies binary messages between the two sockets and reads none of them
relay.backpressure: the server reads from one socket only when the other socket takes the data

channel.transport: TLS 1.3 records in binary relay messages; the viewer is the TLS client
channel.authentication: raw public keys (RFC 7250): the ML-DSA-65 signing key of each device certificate, both sides
channel.viewerCheck: the host key must equal the key of the hosting device in the verified device list of the owner
channel.hostCheck: the viewer key must equal the key of the device that hello names, in the verified device list of the owner or of a person the host shared this terminal with

frames.layout: length:u24be (bytes after this field), type:u8, bodyLength:u24be, body, zero padding
frames.padding: total length up to 1024 bytes: next multiple of 64; larger: Padme

hello.body: JSON: protocolVersion, sessionId, incarnationId, userId, deviceId

refuse.body: JSON: code (version, access, busy, gone), message

keyframe.body: nextSequence:u64be, more:u8, part of the raw deflate of the terminal checkpoint

output.body: firstSequence:u64be, packed:u8, length-prefixed (u32be) chunks, raw deflate when packed
output.packing: each frame alone, from 256 bytes, only when smaller

metadata.body: JSON terminal metadata (directory, title, program, connectedUsers); maximum 16384 bytes

ack.body: received:u64be, the total bytes of keyframe and output frames received

control.body: requestId:16 bytes, JSON control (resize, focus, interrupt, close)

output.start: the first output-carrying frames of a channel are a keyframe; a view never starts in another way
output.sequence: one for each terminal output chunk; keyframe.nextSequence is the sequence of the next output chunk
output.acknowledgement: the viewer sends ack after each 4096 bytes and at most 100 ms after the last frame
output.window: the host keeps at most half a second of output at the acknowledged speed in transit (minimum 16384 bytes, 65536 before the first measurement, maximum 8388608)
output.behind: when output that waits for one viewer is more than the larger of its window and its last keyframe (maximum 8388608), the host drops it for that viewer and sends a new keyframe when all sent data is acknowledged
output.refresh: a viewer can ask for a new keyframe

input.stream: ordered bytes with offsets; the host accepts a frame only at the offset it expects
input.confirmation: inputAck when the terminal accepted the bytes; the viewer keeps at most 65536 bytes without confirmation
input.late: the host refuses input that carries a heartbeat number more than 2 behind its own
input.unconfirmed: when a channel is lost, the view reports the count of bytes without confirmation

controls.result: controlResult for each requestId; a refused control closes no channel

freshness.revocation: the host closes the channels of a person at once when it stops sharing with that person; the server closes the pipes of removed people and devices; other viewers are not affected
freshness.identityReplacement: never silently trust a replacement pinned identity
freshness.tokenExpiry: a connection ends when the access token that opened it expires, unless the device proves a newer token with POST /api/me/connections/renew; the runtime does this after each token refresh
freshness.participantReconnect: a participant runtime keeps its open views when the connection is lost, connects again with a new channel and installs the first keyframe in place
freshness.missingPublicationRecovery: same still-live local session; owner devices only until friends explicitly selected again

presence.source: the host reports the people whose channels it accepted in terminal metadata
presence.meaning: display only; not an authorization grant

termination.order: output that waits is sent before end when the viewer is current
termination.lostConnection: a closed transport without end is a lost connection, not the end of the terminal
